facts.raw_span: dual-chamber pacemaker implantation in the left prepectoral area
an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site
antibiotics (amoxicillin–clavulanate, 1 g three times daily) were started empirically
A swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis
the lesion had darkened and enlarged
dual-chamber pacemaker implantation in the left prepectoral area
an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site
antibiotics (amoxicillin–clavulanate, 1 g three times daily) were started empirically
A swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis
the lesion had darkened and enlarged

concepts.why: The presence of an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site, growth of Staphylococcus epidermidis from the lesion, and progression of the lesion despite antibiotic therapy suggest a pacemaker pocket infection.
The growth of Staphylococcus epidermidis from the lesion and the clinical presentation of the infection suggest a Staphylococcal pacemaker infection.
The presence of fever, elevated inflammatory syndrome, and the initiation of empirical antibiotic therapy suggest sepsis due to device infection.
The progression of the lesion despite antibiotic therapy and the growth of Staphylococcus epidermidis from the lesion suggest a chronic device infection.
The presence of a necrotic lesion and the growth of Staphylococcus epidermidis from the lesion suggest a biofilm-associated device infection.

rationales.F03: Pacemaker implantation increases the risk of device-related infections.
rationales.F05: Fever is a common symptom of infection.
rationales.F06: The presence of an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site is highly suggestive of a device-related infection.
rationales.F07: Elevated inflammatory syndrome is a common laboratory finding in infections.
rationales.F10: The growth of Staphylococcus epidermidis from a swab of the lesion is diagnostic of a staphylococcal device infection.
rationales.F11: Negative blood cultures decrease the likelihood of sepsis due to device infection.
rationales.F12: The progression of the lesion despite antibiotic therapy suggests a chronic or biofilm-associated device infection.
